purpose: Official-source recheck of recent OFD/adamantinoma literature for text-only corpus eligibility and evidence-scope disposition.
method: Checked PubMed/PMC article records and publisher full-text/license pages where reachable. No article payloads or images were downloaded or cached during this recheck.

candidates.title: Osteofibrous dysplasia (OFD) and adamantinoma: A comprehensive review and updates
candidates.observed_metadata: PubMed lists Histology and Histopathology 2026;41(1):11-23, epub 2025-06-13, free article; states © The Author(s) 2025 and Creative Commons CC-BY International License. Abstract describes review scope across OFD clinical/radiological/pathological features and adamantinoma spectrum/differential.
candidates.access_check: PubMed full-text link points to the publisher; retrieval of that endpoint returned HTTP 502 in this check. PubMed does not specify a license version in the displayed statement; no publisher payload or article-level XML was inspected.
candidates.disposition: Follow-up lead only. Do not cache or ingest until full text and exact applicable license version are verified. Do not map review terminology to BTXRD labels.

candidates.title: Osteofibrous dysplasia, osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma, and adamantinoma: A single-center retrospective analysis
candidates.observed_metadata: Journal of Bone Oncology 2025;53:100700. PMC article identifies CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The publisher record describes a single-center retrospective series of 50 patients across OFD, OFD-AD, and adamantinoma.
candidates.disposition: Do not cache or ingest under the project CC BY 4.0 text-ingestion allowlist; retain the existing reviewer lead only. Small, selected cohort; not a reference standard for the project.

candidates.title: Treatment and Management of Osteofibrous Dysplasia Like Adamantinoma – A Single Institution Experience
candidates.observed_metadata: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America 2026;15:100341. PMC article identifies CC BY-NC-ND. The retrospective chart review spans 1958-2016 and reports 59 patients, including small OFDLA and adamantinoma groups.
candidates.disposition: Do not cache or ingest under the project CC BY 4.0 text-ingestion allowlist; retain as a reviewer lead only. Historical classifications and small subgroups limit generalization.

candidates.title: Osteofibrous dysplasia-like adamantinoma: A case report and literature review
candidates.observed_metadata: Frontiers in Oncology 2022;12:967294. Publisher page states Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY). Case report and literature review with imaging and histopathology context.
candidates.disposition: Rights appear compatible for text-only reuse subject to article-level/third-party checks, but no corpus change in this pass: existing OFD review and tibial multimodal review already cover the topic; a single case report is not independent cohort evidence. Reconsider only if a documented retrieval gap warrants it.

limitations: License screening is not legal advice.
No third-party figure rights were assessed; no images are authorized by this review.
These sources do not provide independent validation labels for BoneScope.
No changes were made to source registry, source cache, corpus, vector index, or evaluation gold.
